question: Can jointly optimizing function-preserving symmetry representatives of two pretrained Transformers expose low-loss linear interpolation paths at billion-parameter scale and yield useful merged midpoint models?

key_findings.claim: The framework combines normalization absorption, a global residual-space rotation/scale, attention-head permutations, head-internal QK and OV transforms, and feed-forward permutations/scales.
key_findings.evidence: The paper derives exact affine-normalization absorption, orthogonal global residual reparameterization, head permutation, arbitrary invertible QK/OV changes, FFN permutation, and diagonal GLU value-branch scaling under the stated architecture assumptions.

key_findings.claim: The unrestricted QK transformation is not generally function preserving in the Pythia models used for the language experiments because Pythia applies RoPE after the query/key projections.
key_findings.evidence: The proof preserves unrotated QK products under W_Q M and W_K M inverse-transpose. With position-dependent rotary matrices, the transformed score contains M R_i R_j-transpose M-inverse and equals the original only for transforms commuting with the relevant rotations. The paper acknowledges that RoPE restricts the symmetry but specifies no restriction in its algorithm or Pythia implementation.

key_findings.claim: Endpoint perplexity drift is inconsistent with the claim that every learned transformation is exactly functionality preserving.
key_findings.evidence: For example, Pythia-160M raw endpoint perplexities in Table 7 are 71.19 and 64.09, while the transformed endpoints in Table 6 are 71.27 and 64.67; several other rows also move. Rounding could explain tiny differences, but the systematic changes are not analyzed.

key_findings.claim: Dual learned matching optimizes continuous transforms at both endpoints using loss at a random interpolation coefficient, while keeping discrete assignments fixed after weight matching.
key_findings.evidence: Each step samples lambda uniformly, transforms both checkpoints, linearly interpolates their weights, and backpropagates task loss into continuous Cayley/polar/exponential parameters; attention-head and FFN permutations remain fixed.

key_findings.claim: At the unrestricted symmetry-group level, two endpoint transforms can be rewritten as one relative transform plus a common gauge.
key_findings.evidence: Appendix C algebraically absorbs global, QK, OV, head, and FFN transformations into one single-sided relative group element plus a common function-preserving gauge. This establishes group-level equivalence, not closure of every finite optimization chart used in Table 1.

anchors.section: C, Why dual learned matching works

key_findings.claim: The appendix does not justify its stronger claim that dual parameterization adds no expressivity under the actual Cayley, exponential, and polar charts.
key_findings.evidence: Table 1 explicitly describes restricted chart images, including Cayley matrices without eigenvalue -1 and only the real-logarithm subset of GL+(N). Appendix C proves that relative products remain in the abstract orthogonal or invertible group, but never proves that these chart images are closed under M_B M_A inverse; they generally need not be.

key_findings.claim: Dual learned matching lowers the sampled loss barrier more than raw interpolation, weight matching, and one-sided learned matching across the reported ViT and Pythia panel.
key_findings.evidence: Table 2 reports ViT-S/B/L barriers of 1.11/0.82/0.66 and Pythia-14M/160M/410M/1B barriers of 0.86/0.18/0.37/0.23, all below the listed baselines.

key_findings.claim: The phrase 'near-zero barrier' masks sizable degradation at sampled interior path points.
key_findings.evidence: After matching, ViT-L accuracy falls from endpoints 85.82/82.97 to 69.40 at lambda 0.6 despite a 0.66 loss barrier. Pythia-160M endpoints have perplexity 71.27/64.67 and path values up to 82.47 at lambda 0.4; the 0.18 barrier is small in log loss but not zero in perplexity.

key_findings.claim: Scaling is model-family dependent rather than monotone, so the abstract's claim that modern billion-parameter LLMs have only small barriers does not hold uniformly.
key_findings.evidence: The matched Pythia-6.9B path has loss barrier 0.18 and midpoint perplexity 15.71 versus endpoints 13.22/12.98; OLMo-7B has barrier 1.53 and midpoint perplexity 51.80 versus endpoints 10.83/11.61.

key_findings.claim: A low WikiText interpolation barrier does not preserve downstream Pythia capability.
key_findings.evidence: For 410M, the dual matched/interpolated model scores 55.71 PIQA, 60.00 SciQ, and 35.69 ARC-E versus the original endpoint's 66.43, 81.50, and 51.89. For 1B, it scores 56.42/64.40/37.16 versus 70.95/83.90/56.73. Table 8 does not state the interpolation coefficient, so these values should not be labeled a verified midpoint result.

key_findings.claim: The reported procedure is a substantial data-dependent optimization run, not a simple post-hoc arithmetic merge.
key_findings.evidence: ViTs train symmetry parameters for 100,000 ImageNet steps; Pythia uses 50,000 steps up to 1.4B and 20,000 for 6.9B, while OLMo-7B uses 20,000. Larger runs use four A6000 GPUs for about one day.

key_findings.claim: The experiments show path alignment between similar pretrained checkpoints, not consolidation of complementary capabilities.
key_findings.evidence: Most Pythia pairs are original versus deduplicated training on the same Pile at the same scale; ViT pairs differ in pretraining but are assessed on ImageNet interpolation. No pair is selected for distinct skills, domains, or post-training capabilities, and no capability-union metric is used.

key_findings.claim: Architectural compatibility is a hard scope boundary.
key_findings.evidence: Every pair shares the same layer dimensions, head dimensions, normalization style, and architecture; the approach does not merge different tokenizers, widths, depths, or incompatible modules in the reported experiments.

method.core_idea: Move each checkpoint within its presumed function-equivalence class so that the straight line between the two transformed representatives has low task loss, optimizing both endpoint gauges for better conditioning.
method.mechanism: Weight matching initializes discrete head/FFN assignments. Continuous global and head-internal transforms are parameterized by Cayley, matrix-exponential, or polar forms. Random points on the interpolated weight path are trained on ImageNet or WikiText loss, with both endpoint transform modules updated jointly.
assumptions: The endpoints share exactly compatible architecture, dimensions, tokenizer, and parameter semantics.
Every applied transformation remains function preserving for the actual architecture, including its positional encoding and normalization details.
Optimizing loss on sampled interpolation coefficients generalizes to the evaluated full path.
Low validation loss along a line is a useful proxy for a successful merged model and broader capability preservation.

techniques.role: Produces aligned endpoint representatives and evaluates their linear midpoint or path.
Measures maximum interpolation loss relative to endpoint loss.
Uses discrete and continuous Transformer reparameterizations to align checkpoints.
Overparameterizes one relative symmetry as transforms on both endpoints to improve training geometry.

evaluations.metric: Interpolation loss barrier and top-1 accuracy at lambda intervals of 0.1
evaluations.result: Dual matching gives the lowest listed loss barriers, but worst-path accuracy still falls to 57.10, 63.77, and 69.40 for S, B, and L.
evaluations.baseline: Raw interpolation, weight matching, prior learned matching, and enhanced single-sided matching

evaluations.setting: Pythia original-versus-deduplicated pairs from 14M to 6.9B on WikiText-103
evaluations.metric: Cross-entropy loss barrier and full-path perplexity
evaluations.result: Barriers fall dramatically from raw interpolation; 160M and several larger Pythia pairs have barriers around 0.18-0.23, with nontrivial midpoint perplexity increases.
evaluations.baseline: Raw, weight-matched, and one-sided learned-matched paths

evaluations.setting: HF 1.8B cross-corpus pair and OLMo-7B twin pair
evaluations.metric: WikiText loss barrier and perplexity path
evaluations.result: HF 1.8B reaches barrier 0.55, whereas OLMo-7B remains at 1.53 with midpoint perplexity 51.80.

evaluations.setting: Pythia-410M and 1B zero-shot commonsense check on the matched interpolated model; lambda is not specified
evaluations.result: Dual matching improves substantially over raw interpolation but remains far below original endpoints on all six model-task cells.
evaluations.baseline: Original endpoint, raw interpolation, and single learned matching

evaluations.setting: Symmetry-component and parameterization ablations on ViT-B and Pythia-160M
evaluations.metric: Barrier, worst/midpoint accuracy, and worst/midpoint perplexity
evaluations.result: OV removal hurts both settings; QK removal strongly hurts ViT but has almost no barrier effect on Pythia; polar/Cayley defaults are generally strongest.
evaluations.baseline: Removing QK, OV, global scale, or replacing continuous parameterizations

limitations: Author-stated: endpoints must have compatible architecture and parameter structure.
Author-stated: low WikiText barriers do not imply lossless downstream performance, and only hundreds of millions of symmetry-training tokens are used.
Reviewer inference: unrestricted QK transforms are not exact symmetries under RoPE unless they commute with the rotary representation; the implementation restriction is unspecified.
Reviewer inference: transformed endpoint perplexities drift relative to raw endpoints, contradicting exact functional preservation without an error analysis.

Reviewer inference: Appendix C proves dual-to-single absorption in the abstract symmetry groups but does not prove closure of the restricted Cayley, matrix-exponential, or polar charts used by the optimizer.
Reviewer inference: 20,000-100,000 optimization steps and up to four A6000s for a day make the method closer to retraining a merge adapter than cheap matching.
Reviewer inference: the loss barrier is sampled only at 0.1 intervals for final reporting and can miss narrower maxima.
Reviewer inference: task metrics degrade substantially even when log-loss barriers are called near zero.
Reviewer inference: endpoints mostly do not encode complementary capabilities, so practical capability merging is not tested.
Reviewer inference: Table 8 omits the interpolation coefficient and compares against only one original endpoint, limiting interpretation of its downstream check.
Reviewer inference: the linked official repository still contains only a placeholder README, so the RoPE constraint and numerical endpoint invariance cannot be audited at implementation level.
Reviewer inference: no seed-level uncertainty or independent replication of symmetry optimization is reported.
failure_modes: A purported exact symmetry fails under RoPE or another architecture-specific operation, altering endpoint behavior.
WikiText-trained alignment overfits language-modeling loss while erasing downstream task competence at the midpoint.
The two checkpoints occupy genuinely different functional basins, as suggested by OLMo's high residual barrier.
Discrete weight matching initializes a poor head/FFN assignment that fixed permutations cannot escape.
Continuous invertible transforms become ill-conditioned or restricted parameterizations cannot reach the needed component.
Dual products leave a single chart's image, so an apparent optimization benefit partly reflects chart expressivity rather than only conditioning.
Coarse lambda sampling misses a sharp interpolation spike.
A low-loss average dilutes rather than unites specialized capabilities.
reusable_insights: Audit every claimed symmetry against positional encodings, masks, nonlinearities, normalization, and implementation order—not only the unadorned algebraic block.
Check endpoint function invariance numerically before interpreting path improvements as symmetry resolution.
Distinguish group-level dual-to-single equivalence from chart-level equivalence; explicitly prove closure or compare against a single parameterization that can represent every relative product.
Report both loss-space barriers and human-relevant task metrics across the entire path.
Separate geometric connectivity from capability merging: the latter needs endpoints with complementary skills and union/retention evaluations.
Include symmetry-learning compute in comparisons with naive averaging, soups, task arithmetic, and distillation.
open_questions: What is the exact maximal QK symmetry group for each RoPE layout, partial rotary dimension, and grouped-query architecture?
Do barrier improvements persist when all transforms are constrained and numerically verified to preserve endpoint logits?
Can dense adaptive lambda sampling or adversarial path search reveal hidden narrow barriers?
Can the method merge complementary domain- or task-specialized checkpoints while preserving the union of capabilities?
Why does OLMo-7B resist alignment while similarly sized Pythia appears connected?
Can a cheaper relative-transform optimizer match dual optimization with far fewer task-loss steps?
How much of the dual advantage remains when the single-sided optimizer uses a chart closed under all relative products reached by the dual charts?
Would multi-objective symmetry learning on downstream and safety evaluations prevent the observed capability valley?

competitive_landscape.title: Generalized Linear Mode Connectivity for Transformers
competitive_landscape.relationship: The closest precursor: formulates broad permutation, semi-permutation, orthogonal, and invertible Transformer symmetries and learns low-barrier paths.
competitive_landscape.difference: It supports multi-model and width-heterogeneous alignment and primarily transforms one relative endpoint; this paper scales similar learned symmetry matching and overparameterizes it with transforms on both endpoints.

competitive_landscape.title: Functional Equivalence in Attention: A Comprehensive Study with Applications to Linear Mode Connectivity
competitive_landscape.relationship: The most direct architecture-validity competitor: it formally characterizes attention equivalence with sinusoidal and rotary positional encodings and studies the resulting LMC behavior.
competitive_landscape.difference: It shows that RoPE materially reduces the vanilla attention symmetry group, directly supplying the restriction that this paper acknowledges but does not specify while learning unrestricted-looking QK transforms on Pythia.

competitive_landscape.title: Beyond the Permutation Symmetry of Transformers: The Role of Rotation for Model Fusion
competitive_landscape.relationship: Introduces continuous rotation symmetry for Transformer fusion beyond neuron permutations.
competitive_landscape.difference: It derives a rotation-based matching module across language and vision models; this paper combines more symmetry types, task-loss learning, dual endpoint parameterization, and larger-scale paths.

competitive_landscape.title: Merging Text Transformer Models from Different Initializations
competitive_landscape.relationship: Develops architecture-aware permutation matching for independently initialized text Transformers and evaluates linear barriers.
competitive_landscape.difference: It emphasizes discrete functional-equivalence interventions on smaller masked-LM/fine-tuned models; this paper adds continuous attention/residual symmetries and scales task-loss optimization to billions of parameters.

competitive_landscape.title: Foldable SuperNets: Scalable Merging of Transformers with Different Initializations and Tasks
competitive_landscape.relationship: A practical Transformer-merging competitor that explicitly targets different tasks and initializations using a trained foldable supernet.
competitive_landscape.difference: FS-Merge is not restricted to symmetry-equivalent representatives and pays a distillation-like training cost, but it evaluates complementary multi-task consolidation that this paper's mostly same-corpus path experiments do not test.

competitive_landscape.title: Beyond Structural Symmetries: Linear Mode Connectivity via Neuron Identifiability
competitive_landscape.relationship: A current theoretical alternative that derives approximate equivalence and representation merging from data-dependent neuron identifiability rather than only explicit structural symmetries.
competitive_landscape.difference: It broadens the explanatory route beyond exact Transformer gauge transformations; this paper instead optimizes a hand-enumerated symmetry family on large pretrained checkpoints.

competitive_landscape.title: Linear Mode Connectivity between Multiple Models modulo Permutation Symmetries
competitive_landscape.relationship: Extends permutation-based LMC from pairs to multiple models with a straight-through permutation optimizer and evaluates merged-model loss.
competitive_landscape.difference: STE-MM handles more than two conventional networks but only discrete permutation symmetries; this paper handles two Transformer endpoints with continuous residual and attention transformations at much larger scale.

competitive_landscape.title: Git Re-Basin: Merging Models modulo Permutation Symmetries
competitive_landscape.relationship: Establishes practical permutation alignment and near-zero-barrier merging between independently trained networks.
competitive_landscape.difference: It focuses on permutation gauges in conventional networks and inexpensive matching; this paper targets Transformer-specific continuous symmetries and pays for task-loss training along the path.

novelty_assessment.author_claim: The paper claims the first near-barrier-free connectivity at medium pretrained-language-model scale and a dual learned-matching framework that scales symmetry-aware merging to billion-parameter Transformers.
novelty_assessment.evidence: It combines structured continuous parameterizations, dual endpoint optimization, full sampled ViT/Pythia scaling curves, and larger HF/OLMo tests; dual is consistently lower than the listed one-sided baselines in Table 2.
novelty_assessment.reviewer_inference: The scale-up and dual optimization are useful but incremental extensions of very close generalized-LMC and rotation-fusion work. Functional Equivalence in Attention independently formalizes the RoPE-reduced symmetry group that this method leaves unspecified, and Appendix C proves only group-level—not chart-level—dual equivalence. The practical merging claim remains unestablished because endpoint functions drift, OLMo-7B contradicts a uniform small-barrier story, downstream capability remains poor, the downstream lambda is omitted, and complementary-skill union is not evaluated.

verification.passage_check: Re-read all 18 pages of the pinned arXiv v1 PDF and rechecked every finding against Equations 1-27, the QK/OV proofs, Table 1's parameterization coverage, Algorithm 1, Tables 2-8, Figure 4, the architecture and training-budget appendix, the LayerNorm-to-RMSNorm algebra, Appendix C's full dual-to-single proof, and Appendix F's Cayley/exponential/polar details. All endpoint, path, barrier, training-step, hardware, and downstream numbers were visually re-transcribed; the unsupported midpoint label for Table 8 and the group-versus-chart proof gap were repaired.
verification.competitor_check: Independently checked official current primary records and exact versions for Generalized LMC 2506.22712v2, rotation-based fusion 2502.00264v2, Functional Equivalence in Attention 2606.17830v1, Merging Text Transformers 2403.00986v3, Foldable SuperNets 2410.01483v2, Beyond Structural Symmetries 2606.04754v2, Git Re-Basin 2209.04836v6, and the ICML 2025 PMLR 267 final version of STE-MM; the target was excluded and all URLs, titles, relationships, current revisions, and duplicate constraints were rechecked on 2026-08-23.

reviewer_notes: Completed an independent secondary pass over all 18 cached pages, including every proof, table, figure, endpoint identifier, training detail, limitation, and parameterization appendix. The local source is current arXiv v1. The RoPE contradiction follows algebraically from inserting position-dependent rotations around an unrestricted QK basis change and is independently aligned with the exact-version ICML 2026 functional-equivalence competitor; endpoint perplexity drift corroborates but does not by itself identify the cause. Appendix C's group algebra is valid, but it does not establish closure of the restricted optimization charts. Table 8 never supplies lambda, so the prior reading's midpoint wording was removed. The official linked repository currently contains only a placeholder README stating that code will be released, preventing implementation-level verification of the RoPE restriction and numerical endpoint invariance. Eight current, version-pinned primary competitors were checked.
